content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem now, framing the root cause with appropriate uncertainty since the revert appears not to have fully propagated—logs still show errors with the flag reportedly on. I want the executive summary to focus on user impact and duration rather than specific component names or exact figures already covered.

For timing, I can note it began at 17:42 UTC and hadn't clearly resolved by the last metrics check, treating the duration as a lower bound rather than a precise measurement. I'll list my assumptions and then write out the full postmortem.

assumptions: That the failing account-page requests correspond to real customer-visible failures; this was inferred from error logs and error-rate metrics, not from client-side or business telemetry.

That the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 is the sole driver of the elevated error rate. Only the volume of that error in logs supports this; no code review or trace-level confirmation was done.
That the zero divisor arises from shoppers with, e.g., a zero purchase count. This is a guess at the data condition; nothing in the evidence identifies which value was zero.

That the feature-flag revert at 17:47:58 was actually applied. The logs continued to report the flag as on afterwards, so it is unknown whether the revert failed, propagated too slowly to observe, or propagated correctly while the error persisted for another reason.
That the restart of the summary-cache dependency and the process restarts visible at 17:52 had no bearing on the error rate; no measurement isolates their effect.
That the change history read during the investigation is complete for this service. If flag or config changes were made outside the systems queried, they would not appear.
That the incident remained unresolved after escalation; no post-escalation data was available, so the end time and total impact are unmeasured.
input.executive_summary:
Starting at 17:42 UTC on 26 September 2026, a large fraction of requests to the online shop's account page began failing. Customers trying to view their account would have seen errors; other parts of the shop were not implicated. The failures started when a new spending-summary feature was switched on for customers, and the underlying fault was a defect in the code that feature enables.

Automated response picked the incident up about six minutes after it began and tried three fixes in turn: switching the new feature back off, restarting a supporting internal service, and rolling back the shop to its previous release. None of them worked — the first two did not stop the errors, and the rollback could not run because there was no earlier release to return to. The incident was handed to humans at 17:57 UTC, still broken. The service had not recovered as of the last minute of data available, so the outage lasted at least from 17:42 UTC onward and the true duration and customer impact are not yet known.
input.root_cause: Turning the `monthly-spend-feature` flag on (partial rollout at 17:42, fully on from 17:43) routed account-page requests into a code path that raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 for shoppers with a zero divisor, converting a large share of account-page traffic into errors from the onset minute. This is the best-supported explanation by timing and log evidence, but it is not confirmed: setting the flag back to off at 17:47:58 did not stop the errors and the logs kept reporting the flag as on through 17:56, so either the revert did not propagate or the defect is reachable independently of the flag state; the incident was still open and unexplained when it was escalated.
